I plan to continue working on #13124. I saw elsewhere that the discussion of docs#CovariantClass should not be removed, but it seems to me that custom typeclasses and docs#Covariant should be sufficient.

I’d also like to know whether there are any cases where we genuinely need to distinguish between docs#MulLeftMono and docs#MulRightMono. If we do not need to handle multiplication that is monotone on only one side, we could migrate directly to typeclasses similar to docs#IsOrderedAddMonoid.

Yuyang Zhao said:

it seems to me that custom typeclasses and docs#Covariant should be sufficient.

Agreed, and I would even further say that we don't need Covariant.

Yuyang Zhao said:

I’d also like to know whether there are any cases where we genuinely need to distinguish between docs#MulLeftMono and docs#MulRightMono

Some people care for sure, eg @Hang Lu Su

I have this PR open for left-orderable and right-orderable monoids and distinguishing between docs#MulLeftMono and docs#MulRightMono is important for example for defining bi-orderable monoids.

https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/41505

Would we ever need docs#MulLeftReflectLE without docs#MulLeftMono ? If docs#StrictMono is to be redefined as a ≤ b ↔ f a ≤ f b, then perhaps we should not have mixin typeclasses for LT at all. Instead, we could use typeclasses requiring a ≤ b ↔ c * a ≤ c * b, and also use the new names IsLeftOrderedMonoid and IsLeftOrderedCancelMonoid. This would avoid the issue that docs#mul_left_mono requires docs#MulRightMono as an assumption.
Why is this thread called "TC slowness" btw? There's surely a better name for it
I tend to agree with your diagnosis that LT mixins are useless
7 messages were moved here from #mathlib4 > TC slowness by Yuyang Zhao.
I can only move the 7 most recent messages.
I'm wondering whether IsOrderedCancel* is a good name, since deriving the corresponding IsCancel* instance requires a PartialOrder assumption.
